name: Ilkal Saree
description: Distinctive cotton-silk saree woven with the ancient 'Tope Teni' interlocking technique joining the maroon/red silk pallu with the body. Known for its graceful drape, durability, and traditional motifs.
technique: Pit loom with three shuttles and loop-jointing (Kondi) mechanism
primary_producers: Nekara & Devanga weaving communities; Ilkal Weavers Co-operative
price_range_indicative: ₹1,200 to ₹15,000 (depending on cotton, cotton-silk blend, or pure silk)
source: Official Bagalkote District Portal (Handloom Tourism) & Geographical Indications Registry

name: Guledgudd Khana Fabric
description: Traditional handwoven choli/blouse fabric manufactured exclusively in Guledagudda. Renowned for its structural richness, geometric raised dobby motifs, and deep jewel-tone lustres designed to complement South Indian traditional sarees.
materials_used: Viscose rayon / Silk yarn for extra-warp patterning
technique: Dobby handloom weaving producing raised geometric relief motifs
primary_producers: Guledagudda traditional weaving households; Guledgudd Khana Co-operative
price_range_indicative: ₹350 to ₹2,500 per blouse piece / running meter
source: Official Bagalkote District Portal (Handloom Tourism) & Geographical Indications Registry

name: Kasuti Needlecraft
description: Centuries-old counting-thread embroidery characterized by geometric precision without the use of knots or traced designs, creating reversible designs on temple cloth, sarees, and garments.
gi_status: Registered Geographical Indication under Karnataka Kasuti
craft_base: Badami, Ilkal, and Guledagudda rural clusters
technique: Gavanti (double running stitch), Murgi (zigzag stitch), Negi (weaving stitch), Menthi (cross stitch)
primary_producers: Rural women artisans and self-help collectives
price_range_indicative: ₹500 for small artifacts to ₹8,000+ for heavily embroidered sarees
location: Badami & Hunagund Taluks, Bagalkote District, Karnataka

name: Chalukyan Stone Craft & Relief Carving
description: Living tradition of sandstone and red freestone sculpture practiced in Badami, Aihole, and Pattadakal by traditional Shilpis (stone sculptors) creating temple replicas, miniature pillars, and deity reliefs inspired by Chalukyan rock-cut art.
technique: Hand chiseling according to Shilpa Shastras
primary_producers: Local hereditary sculptor families and artisan guilds
price_range_indicative: ₹300 for small souvenirs to ₹25,000+ for architectural sculptures
location: Badami and Aihole, Bagalkote District, Karnataka
source: Official Bagalkote District Portal & Karnataka Tourism
